analysis.session_summary: The full trading day was risk-off: JPY led majors at +0.48% while NZD lagged at -0.276%; SPX fell 44.3 points and VIX rose 45.0 points, with Brent up 3.085%. Most intraday legs had no clear news catalyst, including EUR/USD's swings and USD/JPY's 144.6-pip range. Late in the day the US Treasury buyback announcements were the clearest measured catalyst, contributing to AUD/USD down 10.7 pips, USD/CAD up 15.9 pips within its leg, and USD/ZAR down 184.5 pips in the first 15 minutes. DXY closed down 37.1 points, leaving the tape dollar-soft against JPY and risk proxies.

themes.evidence: JPY mean vs majors +0.48%; USD/JPY closed -69.9 pips at 153.577; SPX -44.3 points; VIX +45.0 points; Brent +3.085%.

themes.theme: Treasury buyback announcement moved late-day dollar
themes.evidence: AUD/USD leg 16:45-18:45 down -10.7 pips with buyback cause; USD/CAD leg 14:00-18:45 up, buyback +15.9 pips 42% of that leg; USD/ZAR leg 17:00-18:45 down, buyback schedule -184.5 pips first 15 min 87% of leg.

themes.theme: Geopolitical oil risk without clear FX catalyst
themes.evidence: Brent/USD +306.2 pips (+3.085%), high-impact Kharg Island headline at 20:45, but no FX leg had a clear catalyst.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD printed a 33.7-pip range with alternating flows and no single dominant news catalyst; the 16:00 down -28.8-pip leg had nothing on the wire and the 17:00 up move was only halfway pushed by a buyback headline (+6.1 pips, 50% of the move).
leg_notes.GBP/USD: GBP/USD worked a 37.4-pip range with no clear catalyst on any leg, closing +15.4 pips near the middle of its range.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY carved a 144.6-pip range with every leg lacking a clear catalyst, closing -69.9 pips at 153.577.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD ended +2.1 pips after a 27.9-pip range; only the final down leg had a medium-confidence buyback catalyst (-10.7 pips).
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD fell -12.1 pips in a 35.0-pip range with no leg shown as clearly driven.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF closed +7.0 pips in a 42.2-pip range, with no leg having a clear catalyst.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD closed +18.1 pips in a 54.2-pip range; the late up leg was partly driven by the Treasury buyback headline (+15.9 pips, 42% of that leg).

polarity_reads.read: No event cleared the reaction-function threshold; no polarity was measured for any headline, so no inverted/positive read can be reported.

scenarios.name: ECB hawkish signal extends EUR strength
scenarios.thesis: The ECB Main Refinancing Rate is forecast at 2.65% vs 2.40%; if the statement or press conference supports further tightening, EUR/USD can build on its +0.081% daily gain while the dollar stays soft after DXY -37.1 points.
triggers: ECB Main Refinancing Rate prints 2.65% as forecast
scenarios.invalidation: ECB sounds dovish or Core PPI m/m above 0.3% drives a dollar bounce.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD daily range was 33.7 pips; hawkish ECB can push price to the upper end.
EUR/CHF range was 29.8 pips; EUR strength can lift the cross toward its upper range.
GBP/USD daily range was 37.4 pips; dollar softness can support GBP toward the top of that range.
USD/JPY range was 144.6 pips; dollar softness can extend the move lower from 153.577.

scenarios.name: US PPI surprise revives dollar
scenarios.thesis: US Core PPI m/m is forecast at 0.3% and PPI m/m at 0.4%; a hot print after DXY -37.1 points can trigger a dollar rebound, especially against EUR and JPY.
scenarios.invalidation: PPI in line or soft, and the ECB press conference dominates with a hawkish tone.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD daily range was 33.7 pips; hot PPI can push the pair toward the lower end.
USD/JPY range was 144.6 pips; a dollar rebound can lift USD/JPY from 153.577.
USD/CAD daily range was 54.2 pips; USD strength can push it higher within that range.
GBP/USD range was 37.4 pips; a dollar bounce can push cable lower.

scenarios.name: Risk-off deepens on geopolitics/Trump headlines
scenarios.thesis: Brent is already +3.085% and VIX +45.0 points; further Iran or Trump trade headlines can deepen JPY demand and hit high-beta FX while leaving the dollar mixed.
scenarios.invalidation: No new geopolitical headline, oil retreats, and VIX falls below 16.935.

pair_paths.rationale: JPY is the strongest major at +0.48%; risk-off can extend USD/JPY lower in its 144.6-pip range.
CHF/JPY range was 148.3 pips; risk-off favored JPY over CHF, repeating the -102.8-pip daily move.
NZD is the weakest major at -0.276%; risk-off can push NZD/USD lower within its 35.0-pip range.
AUD/USD range was 27.9 pips; high-beta AUD can soften further in risk-off conditions.
